confidence_notes: Beer, coffee, inexpensive meal and mid-range meal are based on searches that found 2026 cost-of-living figures for London from multiple sources. These included a Numbeo-based summary from June 2026 showing about £7.08 for a draft beer, £4.11 for a cappuccino, £20.24 for an inexpensive meal and about £81-85 for a three-course meal for two. Cocktail is based on searches showing about £12-15 at mid-range bars, with cheaper venues at £7-9 and premium venues higher. I set it at about £13.50, but it is less certain. For wine, the searches found only promotional or undated prices and no reliable London average. Wine is therefore a bounded estimate of about £8.50 for a 175ml restaurant glass, based on its usual price relationship to beer in London. Wine is the least certain drink anchor. I converted GBP to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.32 USD/GBP. That rate came from general knowledge, not a search, which adds about ±3% uncertainty. Accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge for July, London's peak season. I did not search them or check live listings. London accommodation prices vary a lot by area and date, so these anchors are less certain than the food and drink anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: London is the comparable basis. Its prices are among the highest in Western Europe, similar to Paris, Dublin and Amsterdam. I adjusted accommodation upward for peak-season demand in July. London drink prices run about 25% above the UK average.
